concepts.title: Definition of Symmetry
concepts.definition: When one part of a figure repeats another part in a regular, predictable way, that repetition is one of the figure's symmetries.
concepts.key_idea: Repetition with a rule: the figure carries a copy of itself inside its own outline.

solution_steps.explain: look for parts that repeat in a definite pattern

describe the repetition rule that makes the figure symmetrical

concepts.title: Line of Symmetry
concepts.definition: Fold the figure along a straight path; if the two sides land exactly on each other, that fold path is a symmetry line.
concepts.key_idea: Folding along this line creates two identical mirror halves.
question_patterns: how many lines of symmetry does this shape have

solution_steps.explain: locate a line that divides the shape into two equal parts
check if the left half exactly fits over the right half when folded
if the halves match exactly, the fold path is a valid line of symmetry

concepts.title: Multiple Lines of Symmetry
concepts.definition: One figure can carry several fold paths at once -- upright, lying flat, or slanted corner to corner.
concepts.key_idea: Regular shapes often possess multiple axes of symmetry.

solution_steps.explain: check for symmetry through the center horizontally and vertically

concepts.title: Reflection Symmetry
concepts.definition: If a fold path lays one side of a figure precisely over the other, the figure shows mirror (reflection) symmetry.
concepts.key_idea: Each point hops to its twin on the far side of the fold, at the same distance.

concepts.title: Rotational Symmetry
concepts.definition: Spin the figure about its middle; if some spin less than a full circle makes it look untouched, it has turn symmetry.
concepts.key_idea: The shape overlaps with itself before a full 360 degree turn.
question_patterns: does this figure have rotational symmetry
find the rotational symmetry of the windmill
identify shapes with rotational symmetry
explain rotational symmetry

solution_steps.explain: find the fixed point around which the object turns
check if the figure looks identical at any angle between 0 and 360 degrees
if the figure matches itself before a full 360 degree turn, it has rotational symmetry

concepts.title: Smallest Angle of Symmetry
concepts.definition: The tiniest spin that leaves the figure looking untouched.
concepts.key_idea: With n identical repeating arms, the tiniest safe spin is one n-th of a circle: 360 / n.
question_patterns: calculate the smallest angle of symmetry

solution_steps.action: identify the number of repeating positions
solution_steps.explain: count how many times the figure overlaps in a full turn
the smallest angle is 360 divided by the number of positions
confirm the remainder is zero -- rotating by the smallest rotation angle makes the figure overlap itself

concepts.title: Angles of Symmetry Multiples
concepts.definition: Every spin that works is a whole-number multiple of that tiniest one.
concepts.key_idea: Tiny spin 90 gives 90, 180, 270 and 360 -- double, triple, and the full circle.
question_patterns: find all angles of symmetry

solution_steps.explain: identify the first rotation that results in overlap
multiply the base angle by integers until 360 is reached
continue multiplying until the full 360 degree turn is reached, then stop

concepts.title: Symmetry of a Circle
concepts.definition: In a circle every straight corner-to-corner path through the middle is a fold path, and every tiny spin is a working spin.
concepts.key_idea: Infinitely many fold paths and spins -- the round shape is the symmetric champion.
question_patterns: how many lines of symmetry does a circle have

solution_steps.explain: any line passing through the center is a line of symmetry
any rotation about the center leaves the circle looking the same
since every diameter is a fold path and every spin works, the circle has infinitely many lines and angles of symmetry
